title: Linear-time unit-Monge distance multiplication
formal: Is there a uniform deterministic \(O(n)\)-time algorithm which, given two permutations \(\pi,\tau\) of \(\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\), returns a permutation \(\rho\) satisfying \(A_\rho(i,j)=\min_{0\le h\le n}(A_\pi(i,h)+A_\tau(h,j))\) for all \(0\le i,j\le n\)?
definitions:
For a permutation \(
u\), define \(A_
u(i,j)=|\{t:i\le t<n,\ 
u(t)<j\}|\). This counting matrix is the implicit simple unit-Monge representation used here. The input is the two permutation arrays, and the output is the array \(ho\); no \((n+1)\)-by-\((n+1)\) matrix is supplied or requested explicitly. The product of two such matrices has a representation of this form. Set \(L=n\ge2\). Use a uniform sequential word RAM with word length \(w=d\lceil\log_2(L+2)ceil\), for a fixed integer \(d\ge 8\) chosen with the algorithm. A fixed finite program must handle every input size; there is no advice, precomputed lookup table or input-dependent oracle. Unit-cost operations are reads, writes, copying, comparisons, branching, Boolean operations, logical shifts, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^w\), and integer quotient and remainder for a nonzero divisor. Shifts by at least \(w\) return zero. Addresses and stored values fit words; multiword operations pay for their constituent instructions. Randomized algorithms, when explicitly permitted, may generate independent uniform random words. All initialization, preprocessing, tables and output writes are charged. A static query starts without input-dependent private state, and every retained copy of the input or auxiliary information counts toward index space. Require \(O(n)\) working words, with all preprocessing charged. All bounds are worst-case with universal constants and no randomness.

context_blocks.text: The matrices summarize many related sequence-comparison values using only a permutation-sized representation.
Tiskin gives an \(O(n\log n)\) algorithm and explicitly attributes the linear-time question to Landau’s question about merging DIST tables.
The ESA 2025 extension to core-sparse Monge matrices retains the same unit-Monge time bound.
The implicit input and output are essential: an explicitly written dense product alone requires quadratic output size.

why: This is a reusable algebraic primitive for semi-local alignment and compressed-string comparison, so a linear bound would affect more than a single query interface.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the same model, quantifiers and resource guarantees. A conditional lower bound establishes only its conditional conclusion. An improvement that does not meet the full target is insufficient.

progress.text: Tiskin establishes \(O(n\log n)\) time for implicit simple unit-Monge multiplication.
The core-sparse generalization matches, rather than improves, this bound in the unit case.

sentences: The input consists of two permutations encoding structured distance matrices.
The output must encode their exact min-plus product.
All three representations have only linear size.
The question asks whether the computation can match that size in time.
The current general unit-Monge bound has a logarithmic overhead.
